objections.claim: DR-002, DR-004, DR-005, and DR-008's integration half are one inseverable Route B selection because they are 'one fact' and selecting Route B for a subset necessarily leaves condition 1 blocked on the same excluded semantics.
objections.evidence: D-001 labels its closure section 'Closure routes, per row.' File 08 gives the four rows different owners and acceptance properties: DR-002 includes AC-1 hostile-input/exit defects, AC-3 claim-register/validator motion, and AC-4 Phase-1A; DR-004 requires the exact Phase-1A packet; DR-005 requires the V10/custody/G19 durable mechanism; DR-008 is already PARTIALLY SATISFIED and retains only its EVIDENCE/D9 integration half. A mixed strategy is lawful: any subset may close by Route A while the rest receive Route B dispositions, satisfying condition 1 row by row. D-019's subset alternative becomes blocked only by assuming the Route A rows never close, which is not an inseparability property. The draft also requires four separate dispositions and admits a later successor may split the cluster, confirming independent invertibility. A common preview rationale does not make four route choices one decision under D-000/D-016.
objections.proposedFix: Make each row's Route B selection independently reviewable and revertible, normally as separate entries/commits, while retaining a shared rationale by reference. If any narrower cluster is claimed inseparable, prove atomicity from the acceptance properties rather than from the fact that all condition-1 rows eventually need a disposition.

objections.claim: The scoped preview threat model covers what the preview actually ships by covering signed delivery, a permission broker, doctor probes, and a bundled Node closure.
objections.evidence: D-002's actual bytes also ship `analyze` as non-interactive project analysis, a TypeScript provider dispatch path, a first-party component process under DR-G21, rebuildable cache/index and operational metadata, and human/JSON plus conditional SARIF output. The enumerated D-020 scope omits the primary attacker-controlled repository/source input, parser/provider protocol and candidate-admission boundary, project-filesystem access, local state, and output/redaction surfaces. A bundled Node closure is a runtime supply-chain asset; it is not a threat model for hostile source text or malformed provider behavior. Because the colon after 'covering what the preview actually ships' presents the four-member list as the scope, the later Route B disposition could be reviewed as complete while omitting the preview's main command and data plane.
objections.proposedFix: Make the listed surfaces explicitly non-exhaustive and require the scoped TM/disposition to cover every D-002 command, input, process/protocol, state, and output boundary. At minimum name hostile repository/source inputs, repository-code execution refusal, TypeScript parser/provider and candidate admission, project filesystem access, cache/index and operational metadata, and output/redaction. Retain the current signed-delivery, permission, doctor, and Node-closure surfaces.

objections.claim: The count-pinned seven steps are attempted 'in this order' while step 7 is a standing parallel lane that starts now and is not sequenced behind steps 4 or 5.
objections.evidence: The intended parallelism is now stated repeatedly and therefore the turn-1 finding landed, but the operative list still gives two incompatible orderings: its preamble makes numeric position authoritative, placing step 7 after steps 1 through 6, while steps 1, 4, 5, and 7 say step 7 starts immediately. A future coordinator can follow the count-pinned order literally and postpone Route A while still claiming compliance. Calling a standing lane 'step 7' is the closing-flourish shape the turn-2 prompt requires this review to attack.
objections.proposedFix: Move the standing Route A lane outside and before the sequential list, or make the first numbered step an explicit two-lane fork. Count-pin the sequential preview lane separately. Do not place an always-active parallel instruction last in a list declared to execute in numeric order.

objections.claim: File-11 item accounting is complete and consistent: only items 1 in part, 2, and 4 are consumed, while item 3 and item 5 remain proposed.
objections.evidence: D-021 step 1 places the DR-117/default-install successor (file-11 item 3) and parallel-product posture (the rest of item 1) into the adopted execution order, and step 5 directs authorship of the non-authoritative analyze contract and fact/finding rule (item 5). The accounting nevertheless calls item 3 and item 5 remaining and calls the posture undecided, while treating mechanically identical step-2 and step-4 scheduling as 'authorization to draft' and therefore consumed. Under D-017, an item becomes live work through an adopted D-000 route and is historical after consumption. D-021 cannot both schedule these items as live work and retain them as an unconsumed file-11 queue.

If inclusion in D-021 authorizes drafting, mark the remaining item-1 half, item 3, and item 5 consumed as authorization-to-draft while leaving their substantive outcomes open at the owning artifacts. Otherwise remove those actions from D-021 until their own entries make them live.
